title: All GTA 6 Radio Stations And Songs
summary:
While the official GTA 6 soundtrack is a behemoth of its own, featuring over 30 tracks of fantastic music, the radio stations you'll tune into while you're cruising around Leonida--or listening in on your phone--are something else entirely. There's a massive list of songs that you can stumble upon, and we've tried to list them all here for you.

As is the case with most of our GTA 6 guides, we'll continue to update this as and when we discover something new. If you've heard something that we haven't included, feel free to let us know.

Worldwide FM

Returning from GTA 5 and Online, Worldwide FM is the one to choose if you like your world music and jazz. Expect to hear:

  • Atmos Blaq - Skhaftin Saka Fonque
  • Cloud One - Atmosphere Strut
  • Dongurizu - Yoppa Ratta
  • Facta ft. Warrior Queen and Killa P - Slope VIP
  • Fejao ft. Samtheman - Brasil de Capoeira
  • Garfield Fleming - Don't Send Me Away
  • Jamiroquai - Smile
  • Moses Ideka & Phil - Do It For You
  • Roberta Flack - The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face

CircoLoco Records Radio

The label that Rockstar co-founded with the Ibiza party in 2021 inspired the name of this station, which plays club bangers including:

  • Skream - Floral
  • Michael Bibi - Rhythm of the Night
  • Mind Against - Let It Go

AfroBank FM

Burna Boy hosts this station with DJ and producer Palms Trax to show off decades of African music including:

  • Tony Allen & The Afro Messengers - No Discrimination
  • Alafia - Assanssan
  • Uncle Waffles - Wadibusa
  • Asake - Joha
  • Pat Thomas ft. Ebo Taylor - Gye Wani
  • DJ Lag & Robot Boii ft. Kamo Mphela - Shay'sana
  • Hugh Masekela - Run No More
  • Manu Dibango - Goro City

Kaleidoscope FM

This is one of the strangest yet best stations in the game. It's hosted by Academy Award winner Jeremy Irons, and mixes interesting covers of songs, global pop, Finnish disco, and more, including:

  • Alim Qasimov & Farghana Qasimova - Say It Right
  • Alkistis Protopsalti - How You Remind Me
  • Marianne Rosenberg - Herz Aus Glas
  • Phuong Thanh - Chia Tay Trong Mua
  • Rolf Bergstrom - Rokkibaby
  • Ron - Hai Capito O No?
  • Trevor M. Simpson & Hi Lo Singers - Stupid Girl

WKTT

Returning from GTA 4, WKTT--or We Know The Truth--is the conservative talk show that features a very apt logo with a bald eagle and flag. The call-in satire you're used to in GTA can be heard here, if you're missing it.

The Wipe

The Wipe is another talk show, focused on the absurdity of the game's world. You'll find some interesting trivia about Leonida here, including some of the more unusual goings on that you might not have stumbled upon yet.

How To Unlock The Vault Radio

The Vault Radio is a secret radio station, but you can unlock it when you get to Vice City. Head to The Vault Nightclub, which you can find pretty much in the middle of Vice City itself. Inside, look for a poster with a pink gas mask on and scan it with your phone. The Vault Radio will now be available for you to listen to, and you can hear all of the dance and electronica tracks that the nightclub itself plays.

title: All Underwater Discoveries In GTA 6 – Kenton’s Treasures Guide
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 will have you exploring the cities and towns of Leonida. But that’s not all: You’ll also be able to swim down to the depths in search of forgotten riches at the bottom of the sea. These activities, known as Underwater Discoveries in the game, are also part of the Kenton’s Treasure’s tally.

In This Article
  • Kenton’s Treasures - Jobs and rewards
    • Underwater Discoveries - How to detect treasure and fend off sharks
    • Shipwrecks off the straits

Kenton’s Treasures - Jobs and rewards

The GTA 6 Kenton’s Treasures activity becomes available during Chapter 1. Simply play through the campaign until you see a mission called Island Dreams. In it, you have to meet up with a captain, Kenton, who charters boat tours for divers.

Note: This mission and all succeeding portions of the activity follow a general structure. Kenton gives you the location of a shipwreck and you have to dive down in search of chests, gold doubloons, and heirlooms. Once you’ve obtained everything, bring them to Kenton in exchange for cash. After a while, he’ll offer a new set of locations for you to investigate.

Underwater Discoveries - How to detect treasure and fend off sharks

During Island Dreams, you’ll be asked to put on a Scuba Gear so you can swim underwater for prolonged periods. Likewise, you’ll receive two tools: The Arras Bullhead and the Metal Detector.

The Arras Bullhead is a harpoon/speargun. Although it doesn’t have a lot of ammo, it still packs a punch. It’s your only defense against sharks that prey on hapless divers.

The Metal Detector, meanwhile, is a device that helps you find sunken riches. Once you reach a shipwreck, bring it out and pan it around until you see a green flash. Keep heading in that direction until the pings become faster. If you’re at the correct spot, you should see an icon/button prompt that lets you grab or pull out the treasure.

Bear in mind that each shipwreck has several relics and coins for you to pick up. Once you’ve found everything, that particular activity is considered complete.

Note: In case you own a different boat outside Jason's house, Kenton will automatically have the Scuba Gear, Arras Bullhead, and Metal Detector delivered to that vessel.

Shipwrecks off the straits

The map below shows the locations of some of the Underwater Discoveries in GTA 6. These are all in the southern portion of Leonida. We’ll keep you posted once we locate other points-of-interest, so stay tuned.

  • Kenton’s Treasure #1: Nuestra Señora del Ocho
  • Kenton’s Treasure #2: Nuestra Señora de la Noche
  • Kenton’s Treasure #3: Nuestra Señora de la Etica Laxa
  • Kenton’s Treasure #4: Nuestra Señora Lujuriosa
  • Kenton’s Treasure #5: Urca de Cinco Torres
  • Kenton’s Treasure #6: Urca de Santa Sierra

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: How To Get A Boat In GTA 6
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 offers a wide variety of vehicles for you to drive in Leonida, including cars, motorcycles, dirt bikes, planes, choppers, and even scooters. However, given the role that water plays on the map, you might be curious about getting a boat fairly early on in GTA 6.

Fortunately, there are a couple of guaranteed ways you can own a boat in Leonida. The ownership comes with a few caveats, though, and you'll also find that boat ownership doesn't work the same as it does with other vehicles, like cars. Below, we'll give you all the details about owning a boat in GTA 6.

Can you own a boat in GTA 6?

At the start of GTA 6, you'll be playing as Jason Duval, and this protagonist can own up to four unique vehicles. You'll get his Granada car by default, and a motorcycle and a kayak if you purchased the Ultimate Edition of the game. Regardless of your edition, though, you'll also have a decent-sized fishing boat ready for you on the dock behind Jason's house in Key Lento.

This boat can be freely used throughout the early part of GTA 6 while Jason is living in Key Lento. Without spoiling anything major, however, you won't be staying in Key Lento forever, and when the story takes you elsewhere, that particular boat won't be able to be recovered.

So, from here, you're left with a couple of options. Unfortunately, in GTA 6, there's no way to register a boat as your own personal vehicle, as you can do with cars, dirt bikes, and motorcycles. No matter what kind of boat you steal or how you acquire it, that boat will never be considered Jason or Lucia's personal vehicle.

Still, this doesn't mean you can't own a boat in spirit.

How to get boats in GTA 6

Naturally, you're absolutely free to steal any boat that you come across in Leonida and dock it in a location that you'll remember. While that particular boat won't always remain there, as it seems that progressing the story wipes out unowned vehicles from their previous locations, you can use this knowledge to store boats nearby when you're free-roaming the map or doing side activities.

There's no "best" spot to steal a boat in GTA 6, as there are dozens of marinas, docks, and other boat storage facilities across the map. The more advanced boats, like large yachts and luxury speedboats, can't be stolen by default, as they all require a Key Cloner. This tool is mostly used to steal cars, but it works on boats as well.

To get a Key Cloner, you'll have to progress through to Chapter 4 when you meet an NPC named Randy. Randy gives a Key Cloner, allowing you to safely steal a wide variety of more advanced vehicles. Other boats, such as smaller and older vessels, can easily be hotwired if you want to take one of those.

For some of the best-looking boats in GTA 6, we recommend going over to the Leaf Links country club, which is found north of Vice City Beach and east of the Decor District. Here, there are several massive yachts just waiting to be stolen, as there's no security around to stop you. You can also head to one of the marinas in Ocean Beach or Washington Beach to find all manner of expensive boats to steal.

If you want to come the closest to owning your boat in GTA 6, though, you'll have to purchase the Ultimate Edition. Starting just after Chapter 4 begins in the story, you'll be able to acquire a custom Shitzu Squalo boat if you're an Ultimate Edition owner. This chunky boat is docked on Washington Island near the Y Hotel, and it remains in its original docking location throughout most of the story.

Aside from those methods, there's no other way to really own your boat in GTA 6. Still, you can have a ton of fun stealing them and riding around the water in a yacht or fast speedboat.

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: GTA 6 Romance Guide: How To Romance Lucia And Jason
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive open-world game on a scale no other game has really tried to bring to life before, but for some players, the romance Lucia and Jason can experience together is all they need. In GTA 6, you can romance Lucia and Jason as you play them both during the game, often getting to switch characters when you prefer to. This means whether you want to romance Lucia as Jason or romance Jason as Lucia, you'll be able to do so. But first, you need to know how to do that. We've played over 100 hours of GTA 6, and we're here to show you how it's done, from going on dates and holding hands to enjoying some--ahem--"hot coffee."

In This Article
  • How to romance Lucia and Jason in GTA 6
    • Optional missions that help with the Lucia and Jason romance
    • Lucia's Release mission
    • Coming Home mission and more romance boosts
    • Jason's and Lucia's relationship/intimacy level
  • How to have sex in GTA 6

How to romance Lucia and Jason in GTA 6

Before the launch of GTA 6, Rockstar detailed how Lucia and Jason's relationship is up to the player to define. Whether they are partners only in crime or in life as well is yours to decide, though it does feel like the game wants you to play it as though they're in a romantic relationship. One of our players said it's  "way harder to make them platonic" and that "you have to really try to push them apart."

For many players, that's fine, because they want to see the pair end up together anyway. To keep them close--and even bring them closer over the 90-hour story--there are a number of things you can do in the game, and, funnily enough, they aren't really that complicated. For anyone in a committed relationship, they'll surely sound familiar. 

Ways to improve Jason and Lucia's relationship include:

  • Holding hands (R2/RT whenever the pair are near each other)
  • Hugging and kissing (hold L2/LT and check for prompts)
  • Spending downtime together and doing activities
  • Driving around together
  • Making conversation when optional prompts appear
  • Most important early on, completing a series of optional missions (detailed below)

Optional missions that help with the Lucia and Jason romance

To that last point in the bulleted list above, there's a series of side missions you can choose to do or not, but doing them will help you start from a stronger place when it comes to romancing GTA 6's Bonnie and Clyde-like couple. We've detailed those missions below, but be warned that they do contain light spoilers, though we've omitted anything we could:

  • Early-game:
    • Fix Jason's house
    • Fix Jason's car
  • Lucia's Release:
    • Get a haircut
    • Buy Lucia a necklace
    • Buy Lucia flowers
    • Purchase groceries and stock the fridge
    • Pick up clothes from Andy

Early in the campaign, you'll notice that Jason's house is in a state that's far from welcoming. You'll need to put in a bit of effort by constructing and painting the bedroom wall, fixing the railings at the back porch, repairing the rooftop, and placing down the steps of the stairs.

Shortly thereafter, you'll receive several missions, one of which requires you to repair Jason's beat up Ganado car. Don't worry as it's completely free the first time around.

Lucia's Release mission

The next five objectives are all tied to the Lucia's Release mini-arc. The establishments and NPCs are marked on your map. Here's a quick summary:

  • Changing your hairstyle and hair color only costs roughly $30, so no worries there.
  • The jewelry vendor sells a gold necklace, which costs $475.
  • The flower shop sells a small bouquet ($5), large bouquet ($10), and roses ($25). You probably want to splurge a bit on the roses.
  • As for the groceries, you can grab all sorts of items from the shelves, including bread, apples, beer, and more. You must bring these over to Jason's house so you can place them inside the fridge.
  • Last but not least, you'll receive a call from an NPC named Andy, who'll inform you that she has some clothes for Lucia. Pick these up and make sure you put them in the Ganado's storage trunk.

Doing these missions in Chapter 1 while you're playing as Jason means that once Lucia joins the story, she and Jason will be in a healthier starting place. Be warned, however, that once you pick up Lucia, these missions will disappear. You must do them before she joins you.

There's no timer to worry about, but if you do miss any, it doesn't mean Lucia and Jason can't end the game in love. It just means you'll have missed out on some early boosts to their intimacy.

Make sure Jason looks clean-cut (left) and stock up on some booze (right).

Coming Home mission and more romance boosts

Once you're all set with the requirements for the GTA 6 Lucia and Jason romance, it's time to tackle the Coming Home mission. Drive the Ganado to the correctional facility to see the two lovebirds reunited. From this point, you should see a few extra boosts to their relationship:

  • An automatic boost once Jason and Lucia hug outside the facility.
  • An off-handed comment upon seeing Jason's car.
  • Act all sweet and romantic at the bar and dance with Lucia.
  • Another automatic boost when Jason fends off an unruly fella.
  • There's also an instance when Lucia finally arrives at Jason's home (assuming you've repaired everything).

Jason's and Lucia's relationship/intimacy level

GTA 6 uses a four-level system to measure how close Jason and Lucia are, with the fourth level signifying you've maxed out their relationship. Note that if you managed to do all the above steps, the couple should be have the "Crazy In Love" status once they're reunited.

title: Can You Romance Mandy In GTA 6?
summary:
There are plenty of memorable moments from the first few hours of the story in Grand Theft Auto 6. From rescuing a friend at a gang hideout to reliving Lucia's run-in with the law, the story certainly isn't dull at any point. However, perhaps the mission that players will remember the most from the opening hours of GTA 6 is "Pipework."

This mission requires you to collect rent money from some of Brian Heder's tenants in Key Lento. One of those tenants is a woman named Mandy, and it's crystal clear from the get-go that she's romantically interested in Jason. So, this begs the question: can you romance Mandy in GTA 6?

Is Mandy romanceable in GTA 6?

While all of the signs point to Mandy being a romance option for Jason in GTA 6, she is actually not able to be romanced whatsoever. This is despite Mandy's best efforts, like when she changes into an extremely skimpy bikini while Jason is fixing her sink.

Throughout your dialogue with Mandy, Jason is never able to steer the conversation in a romantic way. While Mandy will continually flirt with Jason, it appears that Jason is dead-set on making things right with Lucia at this point in the game.

At the end of your time with Mandy, which comes after you fix her sink by removing a curious item that was clogging the pipes, she'll make one last-ditch effort to get Jason to stay. However, once again, Jason refuses, and you have zero control over the situation or whether Jason stays or not.

While you'll eventually have to leave Mandy to progress the Pipework mission, that doesn't mean you can't return to her at a later point in GTA 6. However, even if you return to Mandy's home, she won't be in the mood for any kind of romance. Returning to her home finds her crying in front of the TV, and if she spots you, she'll tell you to go away, as Jason has seemingly broken her heart.

Beyond this, there are no further interactions with Mandy in GTA 6, even if you decide not to pursue a romantic relationship with Lucia when she gets out of prison. Speaking of which, if you want to find out about actual romance options in GTA 6 and how to get Jason and Lucia together, take a look at our other guide. We've also covered whether Jason and Lucia can go on dates together if you're in the mood for some more romance.

For more on Jason and Lucia, or how to find some of the biggest secrets in the game, check out our GTA 6 guides hub.

title: The New, Non-GTA 6 Games You Should Be Playing Right Now
summary:
While Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to dominate what GameSpot covers for the next month (at least), it doesn't mean there aren't plenty of other games out there that those of us are playing at the same time (or in the cases of those of us who aren't big GTA fans, what we're playing instead). Whether it's a new demo for a game we're eagerly anticipating, an indie title that's bravely facing off against Rockstar's juggernaut of a title, or just something that made us smile, we want to take a chance to highlight those games too.

Below, you'll find a list of smaller or lesser-known games that we're playing alongside or instead of GTA 6, as well as links to our coverage of those titles. As we get into the thick of Grand Theft Auto 6 season, we'll keep coming back here to add additional impression pieces we want to highlight.

    • Village in the Shade

Memorable Demos

A fantastic demo can reinforce your decision to go ahead and wishlist or preorder a game you already have your sights on, but the best-of-the-best are those that surprise. Sometimes you have no idea what a game is going to be like or whether you'd even like it, and then you try out the free demo at the last in-person E3 you ever attended and suddenly the game becomes your entire personality for the next six years.

Over the past month or so, we've played demos in both camps. None of these games are out yet, but they're all scheduled to launch either later this year or sometime next year. If you've got a spare hour or two, these snippets are an excellent way to spend your time.

At Fate's End

My most anticipated game of 2026 was At Fate's End. I say "was" because it was delayed to 2027. Thankfully, a demo for the game was released alongside the announcement of the delay, allowing me to at least experience a morsel of what's to come. Spoiler: It's fantastic. This is the next game from Spiritfarer developer Thunder Lotus, which sees you embody the role of a warrior princess who has to duel her hurting siblings with sharp swords and even sharper words--it's the exact emotional devastation I crave. And both the art and music direction are nothing to sneeze at. This is a pretty game to both look at and listen to.

Draftula

So you took GameSpot editor Steve Watt's wonderfully written Castlevania: Belmont's Curse review to heart, bought the game, and enjoyed fighting Dracula as yet another member of the Belmont family. But now what? Well, you could go help rebuild Dracula's castle in preparation for the next invasive adventurer. Writer Dave Irwin enjoyed the demo for Draftula, an upcoming roguelite that sees you needing to build Dracula's misshapen castle over and over, higher and higher, in order to waylay any would-be heroes.

Exterminauts

Okay, technically not a demo, but a beta test that you can join right now is demo-ish. GameSpot editor Mark Delaney compares Exterminauts to Helldivers 2, although this three-person player-versus-environment shooter stars regular schmucks obsessed with do-it-yourself projects, not patriotic starship troopers. The game otherwise plays very similarly to Helldivers 2, so the beta feels more like a means of testing to see whether the narrative flavor is to your liking. If you already like Helldivers 2, you'll probably like the gameplay of this shooter too.

My Arms Are Longer Now

GameSpot managing editor Chris Pereira and I often muse in our weekly one-on-one meetings that we rarely have time to destress via gaming, since the portal by which we primarily play games is also the machine we sit at all day for work. So any weird game that gets Chris to relax makes me happy and is more than deserving of a shout-out. My Arms Are Longer Now is a bizarre game that's strangely compelling--between the ridiculous humor of controlling an arm that stretches belief and the silly hijinks that you're able to get up to, this will likely remain the funniest demo in this roundup. 

Nirvana Noir

Genesis Noir is one of the most memorable games of 2021. Its use of abstract art to frame a compelling noir detective story within the explosion of the big bang created an experience that was quite novel. The next game, Nirvana Noir, aims to tell an even weirder story. Writer Khee Hoon Chan likes how the vibrant color of Nirvana Noir makes for an eye-catching sequel, one in which a detective hops between parallel realities (one in which the Big Bang happened, and one in which it didn't) to unravel a conspiracy centered around the final moment of Genesis Noir. The game looks gorgeous, and the demo already indicates that this game's puzzles and mysteries are going to be just as spellbinding as the first game.

Paranormal Activity: Threshold

Mark puts it perfectly: The scariest game of the year is a demo for a game that isn’t even coming out. Like Silent Hills before it (and Devotion seemingly until it surprisingly did come back), Threshold is a fantastically spooky good time that's just never going to release in full. But at least we still have this great demo to experience a tiny glimpse of what was going to probably be a strong first-person horror game. It's really no big surprise that this demo is good--Threshold was being developed by DarkStone Digital, the same studio behind the extremely popular (and oftentimes way too scary for me) The Mortuary Assistant. 

New Releases

There aren't just new demos to play right now. Some studios are bravely staring down the Goliath that is Grand Theft Auto 6, the sling that is their much smaller title in hand. Releasing in the weeks leading up to GTA 6 or in the weeks post-GTA 6's launch is a bold choice, but those of us who aren't huge into sandbox games are thankful that they're here. Too much of just one thing for a long time isn't always fun.

These games fall into their own niche--you're not going to find any games listed here that feel like GTA 6 but smaller. We imagine most of those games were delayed to 2027 or beyond in order to not be overshadowed by Rockstar's action-adventure.

Australia Did It

A fear of being spoiled on GTA 6's story is pushing Chris to try and focus on Rockstar's action-adventure game, but a very different game has been slowly clawing its way into his heart. Between its fun unit-combining mechanics and hilarious conveyor belt of doom, Australia Did It has been pulling Chris away from GTA 6. Part turn-based tactics game, part tower-defense game, part survivorslike, Australia Did It seems tailor-made for GameSpot's resident tactics aficionado, but don't let Chris have all the fun. Be sure to check out this game yourself!

Deadlock

Deadlock is the latest in a now dwindling field of hero shooters, but unlike the swing-and-a-miss mishaps of Concord and Highguard, Deadlock seems to have the juice to stick around. The game's player numbers saw a huge surge in September with the City Never Sleeps update, and it's basically been doing just fine ever since despite technically still being in early development. Fingers crossed that continues to be the case. Deadlock has some of my favorite lore of any shooter ever, which is only amplified by the impressive world design of its maps and phenomenal character art direction. Writer Ana Diaz said that Deadlock is the game that convinced her we should all be role-playing in competitive games, and after seeing so many people doing just that in Deadlock and posting those conversations on YouTube, I'm inclined to agree!

Hunger

Unlike most of these games that are releasing just before GTA 6, Hunger is scheduled to launch just after Rockstar's game comes out. Set to be released in Steam Early Access on December 3, Hunger is an extraction role-playing game in which you navigate a plague-stricken Napoleonic Europe (so weird that we got two first-person zombie-adjacent Napoleon-centered games in 2026). If you're anything like me, you see the words "extraction shooter" and want to log off, but hold on! After playing Hunger for eight hours, writer Cameron Koch points to the extraction RPG's promise of permanent progress as its most compelling feature. You're doing everything else you would in other extraction games--looting, encountering other players, trying to get away--but there's a bit of roguelite-inspired gameplay at work here too, ensuring you can retain permanent upgrades not only from run-to-run, but season to season. 

Tanuki: Pon's Summer

A bike-riding, mail-delivering raccoon dares to challenge GTA 6, and we should all support him. Mark played this game in the week leading up to GTA 6's launch and spoke with game director Liam Edwards as to how the team decided that releasing their third-person adventure game between The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6 was the right move. Blending together BMX tricks and Japan-inspired locales, Pon's Summer sees the titular tanuki racing through four cities to deliver the mail as quickly (and as cool) as he can. 

Thank You Bus Driver

Friendslop is all the rage these days but, as the name implies, you do need friends to play with in order to enjoy them. Or I guess you could cheat like Mark and just have children. But not all of us are so lucky to be blessed with the circumstances to create people to play games with. That's what writer Jade King enjoys most about Double Fine's Thank You Bus Driver--this wacky first-person driving adventure game feels like playing friendslop, but it's single-player. The game sees you playing as the titular bus driver and utilizing 1930s animation logic to safely get your passengers to their destination--stretching your arms to absurd lengths to smack troublemakers in the back of the bus, for example, or utilizing magical trinkets to transform how the bus handles.

Queen's Domain

Quite a few of us at GameSpot are obsessed with Queen's Domain--it's quickly gone from a "I'll try to play this game at some point" to "I should play this before GameSpot's Best Of deliberations." GameSpot senior video producer Jean-Luc Seipke first put the game on our radar with their argument that Queen's Domain is gonna be a cult classic. Really hard to argue that I don't need to check out a game with a statement like that. But the pressure to check this game out only grew when Jade added that Queen's Domain has the most terrifying mimic ever, and that the whole game just has some of the best enemy creature design of any action-adventure game this year. You should join me in trying out this game this November.

Village in the Shade

First released in Japan on July 30, Village in the Shade released in North America and Europe more recently on October 30. Featuring a hand-painted art style and cute-looking characters, Village in the Shade looks like another in a long line of relaxing farming sims. But it's not. Instead, this game is another in a long line of "looks like a cozy game but is 100% not." Your farmer is immediately inundated with strange rules: don't talk to strangers and don't go out after 11 PM, among other similarly strange limitations. When writer Heidi Kemps checked out the game, she noted that it doesn't take long for Village in the Shade's otherworldly, encroaching horror to take hold, and you can't help but want to unravel the mounting mystery of the town.

These games fall into their own niche--you're not going to find any games listed here that feel like GTA 6 but smaller. We imagine most of those games were delayed to 2027 or beyond in order to not be overshadowed by Rockstar's action-adventure.

Australia Did It

A fear of being spoiled on GTA 6's story is pushing Chris to try and focus on Rockstar's action-adventure game, but a very different game has been slowly clawing its way into his heart. Between its fun unit-combining mechanics and hilarious conveyor belt of doom, Australia Did It has been pulling Chris away from GTA 6. Part turn-based tactics game, part tower-defense game, part survivorslike, Australia Did It seems tailor-made for GameSpot's resident tactics aficionado, but don't let Chris have all the fun. Be sure to check out this game yourself!

Deadlock

Deadlock is the latest in a now dwindling field of hero shooters, but unlike the swing-and-a-miss mishaps of Concord and Highguard, Deadlock seems to have the juice to stick around. The game's player numbers saw a huge surge in September with the City Never Sleeps update, and it's basically been doing just fine ever since despite technically still being in early development. Fingers crossed that continues to be the case. Deadlock has some of my favorite lore of any shooter ever, which is only amplified by the impressive world design of its maps and phenomenal character art direction. Writer Ana Diaz said that Deadlock is the game that convinced her we should all be role-playing in competitive games, and after seeing so many people doing just that in Deadlock and posting those conversations on YouTube, I'm inclined to agree!

Hunger

Unlike most of these games that are releasing just before GTA 6, Hunger is scheduled to launch just after Rockstar's game comes out. Set to be released in Steam Early Access on December 3, Hunger is an extraction role-playing game in which you navigate a plague-stricken Napoleonic Europe (so weird that we got two first-person zombie-adjacent Napoleon-centered games in 2026). If you're anything like me, you see the words "extraction shooter" and want to log off, but hold on! After playing Hunger for eight hours, writer Cameron Koch points to the extraction RPG's promise of permanent progress as its most compelling feature. You're doing everything else you would in other extraction games--looting, encountering other players, trying to get away--but there's a bit of roguelite-inspired gameplay at work here too, ensuring you can retain permanent upgrades not only from run-to-run, but season to season.

A bike-riding, mail-delivering raccoon dares to challenge GTA 6, and we should all support him. Mark played this game in the week leading up to GTA 6's launch and spoke with game director Liam Edwards as to how the team decided that releasing their third-person adventure game between The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6 was the right move. Blending together BMX tricks and Japan-inspired locales, Pon's Summer sees the titular tanuki racing through four cities to deliver the mail as quickly (and as cool) as he can. 

Thank You Bus Driver

Friendslop is all the rage these days but, as the name implies, you do need friends to play with in order to enjoy them. Or I guess you could cheat like Mark and just have children. But not all of us are so lucky to be blessed with the circumstances to create people to play games with. That's what writer Jade King enjoys most about Double Fine's Thank You Bus Driver--this wacky first-person driving adventure game feels like playing friendslop, but it's single-player. The game sees you playing as the titular bus driver and utilizing 1930s animation logic to safely get your passengers to their destination--stretching your arms to absurd lengths to smack troublemakers in the back of the bus, for example, or utilizing magical trinkets to transform how the bus handles.

Queen's Domain

Quite a few of us at GameSpot are obsessed with Queen's Domain--it's quickly gone from a "I'll try to play this game at some point" to "I should play this before GameSpot's Best Of deliberations." GameSpot senior video producer Jean-Luc Seipke first put the game on our radar with their argument that Queen's Domain is gonna be a cult classic. Really hard to argue that I don't need to check out a game with a statement like that. But the pressure to check this game out only grew when Jade added that Queen's Domain has the most terrifying mimic ever, and that the whole game just has some of the best enemy creature design of any action-adventure game this year. You should join me in trying out this game this November.

Village in the Shade

First released in Japan on July 30, Village in the Shade released in North America and Europe more recently on October 30. Featuring a hand-painted art style and cute-looking characters, Village in the Shade looks like another in a long line of relaxing farming sims. But it's not. Instead, this game is another in a long line of "looks like a cozy game but is 100% not." Your farmer is immediately inundated with strange rules: don't talk to strangers and don't go out after 11 PM, among other similarly strange limitations. When writer Heidi Kemps checked out the game, she noted that it doesn't take long for Village in the Shade's otherworldly, encroaching horror to take hold, and you can't help but want to unravel the mounting mystery of the town.

title: Fortnite’s Treasure Hunt Burned Me Out Just In Time For GTA 6
summary:
I'm a male Millennial gamer pushing 40, so GTA is in my bones. But I currently like Fortnite more than I like any other game, and I figured I'd have a hard time pulling myself away even for an occasion as momentous as the arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6--especially after Epic announced the big One Piece-themed treasure hunt with oodles of free cosmetics at stake, including cars, Jam tracks, a token that lets you get the whole item shop free, and ultra-rare gold skins that you'll probably never be able to get any other way. That kind of stuff is catnip for a longtime Fortnite player like me, and it got me playing a lot more than I usually do. After a couple weeks, though, the treasure hunt has burned me out so thoroughly that I'm excited to get the hell out of Fortnite for a while. 

The treasure hunt has been a huge success, though--player numbers went through the roof, and the hunt drove up the length of the average session--and the trick worked on me just as well as it worked on everyone else. Fortnite Tracker says I've played 60 hours of BR this season, which is ludicrous. If this season were as long as last season, I'd be on pace for more than 250 hours played--which would outstrip my previous most-played season by more than 100 hours. I've been playing, ah, pretty obsessively.

But the treasure hunt has broken me, and I don't want to play Fortnite any more right now. And it's not only because I've been playing too much. People are behaving very strangely in pursuit of the treasure, and so it's hard to just have a regular game of Fortnite--that's an unfortunate thing, because this would be an all-timer of a season if people were playing normally. Since I myself am also distracted by the treasure, spending more time looking for chests than I do other players, I've been playing poorly and not enjoying fights as much as I normally do. Competing and winning are not the highest priorities for most players right now, and it's made everything weird.

And on the rewards side of this hunt, the treasure is too sparse. In addition to the Pirate Shop token, which is available all season, each week offers four unique treasure items that are only available for that week: a Jam track, one accessory (back bling or pickaxe), a car skin, and a gold character skin. The Jam tracks and accessories are very common and most players will earn them within an hour or two of playing each week, and the cars are a bit harder to find but still fairly accessible. But the odds on the shop token are so low (1:137k) that very few people will find it, and the gold skins actually have even worse odds (1:1.5m). It's hard to be a winner here.

With the odds stacked so heavily against us, I've gone days at a time without finding anything other than worthless gizmos, and my last straw was a new "feature" Epic introduced this week that allowed folks to find duplicate treasures if their squadmates didn't already have them. It's a good idea in theory, because you don't want to make it harder for people to get the treasures just because they're playing with somebody who already has them. 

But it was pretty psychologically devastating on Monday to see a chest do the treasure animation, and expect to receive one of the ultra-rare items--the shop token and the weekly gold skin were my only remaining treasures--and then not get anything at all from it. It was brutal, and it killed my remaining motivation. I never actually wanted that pirate token or the gold Miku anyway! Or at least that's what I'm trying to tell myself.

The timing is funny, coming just a couple days before GTA 6 launches. Epic is ostensibly doing this whole treasure hunt as counterprogramming for GTA 6, which is going to be the biggest video game launch of all time. At the start of the season, I thought the treasure hunt might actually be worthwhile enough to keep my attention even after GTA launched. Obviously, I was going to play GTA no matter what, but I kinda assumed it would be another game I play in between Fortnite sessions, like the other single-player games I play usually are. Instead, the treasure hunt burned me out so efficiently that it's looking like the opposite will end up being true, for at least a couple months: Fortnite will be what I play when I need a change of pace from GTA.

Five years is a long time to stick with one game, so it'll be refreshing to switch my main focus to something else, whether it's temporary or permanent. Also, Epic's open enthusiasm for vibe coding everything and AI slop seems likely to break Fortnite sooner than later, or at least turn it into something I enjoy a lot less than I have in the past. 

So maybe it's for the best that GTA 6, which so far has the highest Metacritic score of any game ever, is giving me the opportunity to move on without any regrets.

title: GTA 6’s Best Song Is A Nelly Furtado Cover From Azerbaijan
summary:
One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones. As a music-discovery vehicle, GTA: Vice City introduced me to many '80s classics across a variety of genres. With GTA 6 taking players to Leonida, in which Vice City is located, it's apt that the game features music that many probably would never hear anywhere else.

One of the radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM. It features covers of very-well-known songs that are performed by artists from around the world. It's a fantastic hook for a radio station and delivers some of the catchiest and most-unexpected covers from artists that have a pretty low profile outside of their home countries.

The first song I heard on the station, and the one that remains my absolute favorite, is a cover of Nelly Furtado's "Say It Right" from Azerbaijani artists Alim Qasimov and Farghana Qasimova. The duo are known for performing Mugham, a type of music that blends poetry, melody, and improvisation. I had never heard of them before playing GTA 6, but the music instantly transported me to my youth listening to Qawwali, a type of music that is rooted in Islamic sufism. 

Initially, my exposure to Qawwali, a type of music that is over 600 years old, was limited to my own home, but it has since gained a worldwide following thanks to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, who is known as the King of Kings of Qawwali. These days it's pretty common to hear songs that either sample or are inspired by Qawwali, but, even so, hearing Mugham in GTA 6 was a huge surprise. I didn't expect to be playing Rockstar's latest opus and be reminded of Qawwali.

I already love "Say It Right"--I think it's one of Furtado and producers Timbaland and Danja's best--but this cover draws out the melancholic soul that underpins the original, giving it a more emotional weight. Much of that can be attributed to the religious mysticism that both Mugham and Qawwali evoke. 

What I appreciate about this cover is how brilliantly it allows the unfamiliar to grasp what makes Mugham and Qawwali so beautiful by presenting it through a song that many people already have some familiarity with. Both types of music are performed by an ensemble, but the improvisational nature means that others are encouraged to contribute. The use of the kamancheh, tar, and daf, along with the vocals covering Furtado's chorus and the khananda's additions, come together to make the cover feel magical. 

There are other songs that will no doubt catch you by surprise on Kaleidoscope FM--another favourite is a South Asian cover of "Careless Whisper." Naturally, I was intrigued by how this station came to be and, according to Ivan Pavlovich, Rockstar's vice president of music, it stems from an obsession that studio co-founder Sam Houser has.

“Historically, we have always loved to champion a quirky, concept-driven station," Pavlovich told GameSpot. "Sam loves foreign-language covers of his favorite songs and thought this could be that station for GTA VI. Tracking down rights holders proved particularly tricky in certain countries."

The biggest surprise, however, is the radio station's host: Academy Award winner Jeremy Irons.

"Jeremy Irons has the perfect voice as the travel-weathered host telling tall tales of his adventures from around the world," Pavlovich added. "Jeremy loved the script, and nailed the wry humor of his character in one session. Hopefully, this station makes fans smile as much as we did when we were making it."

Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are available now. GameSpot gave it a 10/10, saying that it sets the standard for open worlds impossibly high.

title: PSN Went Down Sorta On GTA 6 Eve
summary:
On the eve of GTA 6's official launch on November 19, Sony's PlayStation Network appears to be facing some issues, at least for some people, at some point, today.

Reports have emerged that the PSN is borked, and although the PlayStation Status website says everything is fine, that might not be true for everyone.

As with all outages, your mileage may vary. It was reported that the PSN had a temporary outage for launching games specifically, and this has since been fixed.

GTA 6 is expected to put enormous strain on PSN and the Xbox Network as millions of people log in to play. GTA 6 is already live and playable in New Zealand, Australia, and other parts of the world, but those places are not where the majority of gamers are.

Keep checking back with GameSpot for more on how online networks are holding up as GTA 6 approaches.

GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. For now, you can read GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

title: GTA 6 Easter Eggs Are Everywhere, But These Are The Best Ones
summary:
GTA 6 Easter eggs are everywhere, it feels like. We've only just begun gathering them in this roundup, and it feels like there are so many more.

From books and store items to little nods in the dialogue or places of interest, Grand Theft Auto 6 is as much an amalgam of pop culture as it is a hyper-realized funhouse mirror of US culture.

We'll be regularly adding more GTA 6 Easter eggs to this article, so keep it bookmarked as you set off for your very long playthrough of GTA 6. 

In This Article
  • Red Dead Redemption reminders
  • The Liberty City saga continues
  • Dexter Morgan's apartment
  • A literal Easter egg
  • Bigfoot is back

Red Dead Redemption reminders

Location: various, but the one pictured is in Jacob's Tavern in Millport

Across the huge GTA 6 map, there are several reminders that Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto share a single story universe. One of the earlier ones you might see is a Western novel that tells the story of a cowboy living in New Austin, a location from the Red Dead Redemption series. 

Even cooler, you can read excerpts from books and magazines in GTA 6, so if you find this one, be sure to read the text to immerse yourself in what is technically Rockstar's latest Wild West adventure.

The Liberty City saga continues

Location: various, but the one pictured is on Jason's dining-room table early in Chapter 1

If you didn't know Red Dead and GTA share one universe, you probably at least knew Liberty City, Los Santos, and Vice City do. Early on when you start to play as Jason, you can roam freely around his home. 

There's literature to check out all over the property, but the one on his small table near his back door is a memoir from a former member of Liberty City's organized crime ring. Within the pages, the writer even references events from 2008, seemingly signaling that Rockstar is calling out how that book ties directly to GTA 4, which is set in 2008.

Dexter Morgan's apartment

Location: Washington Island, near the Vice Beach Top Fun Drones shop is located

The Bay Harbor Butcher may be lurking somewhere in Leonida, since his apartment certainly is. We've already broken out a full guide on how to find Dexter Morgan's apartment in GTA 6, but if you want the shorter version, you can head to Washington Island, which is a subregion of Vice City itself. You won't get to Vice City for a while if you wait for the story to take you there, though you are free to head there sooner if you want to.

You can't get into the apartment, meaning you can't check inside his air conditioner for his kill trophies, sorry to say. However, some players think the boat docked nearby looks a lot like Dexter's beloved Slice of Life.

A literal Easter egg

Location: Atop the tallest tower in Vice City

While each of the listings in this article is considered an Easter egg, only one of them is truly that. This Easter egg is found by scaling a tall tower in Vice City proper, which the player who found it and shared it online said took about seven minutes. At the top, Jason or Lucia can take the Easter egg from the nest and throw it. 

We won't spoil what happens next. You should really see it for yourself, but if you don't mind the spoiler, check out the stunning conclusion here.

Bigfoot is back

Location: Gullet Marsh

Rockstar's fans have been obsessed with Bigfoot mysteries for many years now, though in GTA 6, the hairy fella gets the type of spotlight he's not had before: He's unmissable thanks to a particular mission that sees you have a close encounter with him.

Of course, if you don't want to see it before you do so on your own time, don't read any more about it. But like the Easter egg above, there's more to be seen if you'd like to see it. Does it count as an Easter egg if it's unmissable? Not usually, but given the history surrounding this one, we're including it anyway.

Stay tuned for lots more Easter eggs that will be added here over time.

For everything else related to the biggest game of the decade (century? ever?), use our GTA 6 guides hub.

title: KFC Announces GTA 6 Promo Where You Get A Disc-Shaped Piece Of Chicken
summary:
A lot of people are upset that they can't get GTA 6 on a physical disc, and KFC is now stepping up to do what Rockstar isn't.

KFC Spain has announced a "Replace the Disc" campaign where customers can get a free disc-shaped piece of fried chicken when they bring in their GTA 6 box. The promotion takes place December 19 and 20 from 4 to 8 PM at KFC locations in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, and others in the country.

GTA 6 is sold at retailers like Best Buy, GameStop, and Target, but the box doesn't include a disc--instead, you get a code to unlock the game. GTA 6 owner Take-Two recently reported that 98% of its sales were digital, and while there will be some physical aspects to gaming forever, it's an increasingly small part of the business, Take-Two's boss has said.

This is not KFC's only promotion for GTA 6. KFC Australia is holding a fake funeral for a person named "Ann Alibi" in Australia's version of Miami on November 19. The fake funeral services are taking place in the middle of the day, per Ann's wishes, and so that people can have a "legitimate" reason to take the day off.

Numerous brands are latching onto GTA 6 to leverage the enormity of the game's release to promote their own stuff. McDonald's, for example, just announced a campaign to get your McNuggets or Big Mac delivered while you keep playing GTA 6. Even smaller, more regional brands--including the Massachusetts-based brewery Tree House--have announced GTA 6 promos.
